name: SIA Project 25 26
description:
In the Municipality of Turin, a system called Participium is being developed — an information 
system that enables citizen participation in the management of urban environments. It allows 
citizens to interact with the public administration by reporting inconveniences and malfunctions 
found in the city (e.g., potholes in the asphalt, sidewalks with architectural barriers, garbage in the 
streets, broken streetlights, etc.). An example of a similar information system is IRIS in Venice: 
https://iris.sad.ve.it/. The system, once developed, will be made available as open-source 
software to all Italian public administrations through the portal https://developers.italia.it/.

A. REPORTS 
Citizens can submit reports only if they have registered in the system with a username, first name, 
and last name. Once the registration is received, the user gets an email with a confirmation link. 
The registration becomes valid, and the user can use the system only after confirming through 
that link. Once registered, a citizen can submit reports by selecting a point on the map of Turin 
(which will be saved with latitude and longitude values) and filling in a problem form with the 
following mandatory fields: title, textual description, category (chosen from a predefined list). It is 
also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report, with each photo stored with its 
file path on the server). The possible problem categories are: 
• Waterworks – Drinking water 
• Architectural Barriers 
• Sewerage 
• Public Lighting 
• Waste 
• Road Signs and Traffic Lights 
• Roads and Urban Furniture 
• Public Green Areas and Playgrounds 
• Other 
After entering all the information and the pictures, the system asks the citizen whether they want 
the report to be anonymous (the name will not appear in the public list of all reports).  

B. REPORT LIFECYCLE 
Once submitted, the report is in the “Pending Approval” state until the Organization Office of the 
Municipality of Turin performs a preliminary review of citizen reports, marking them as accepted 
or rejected. The possible states for a report are: Pending Approval, In Progress, Work in Progress, 
Suspended, Rejected. After approval, accepted reports move to the “In Progress” state, at which 
point they are assigned to the technical office responsible, based on the problem category. Once 
the intervention is planned, the state changes to “Work in Progress”, indicating that the issue 
resolution has started. In some cases, for organizational or technical reasons, the report can be 
set to “Suspended”, awaiting further evaluation or resources. When the problem is solved, the 
technical office updates the status and closes the report. In case of rejection, a written explanation 
from the Organization Office is mandatory (see next section).  
If the intervention must be carried out by maintenance personnel from an external company (for 
example, Enel X for Public Lighting, or company Y for specific reports based on their content), 
two cases are possible: - Case 1: The company has access to Participium. In this case, the technical office assigns the 
report to users from the corresponding company. External maintenance personnel can move the 
report from Assigned to In Progress. Staff from the technical office and external maintenance 
workers can exchange information and comments through the report, but these are not visible to 
the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens). Once the work is completed, the external maintainer 
can mark the report as resolved. 
Note: Automatic assignment of all reports in a certain category to the external company 
(bypassing the initial review by the public relations officer of the municipality) is possible only if 
previously configured by the municipal administrator. - Case 2: The company does NOT have access to Participium. In this case, the external company 
updates the technical office outside Participium, and once the problems are solved, a staff 
member from the technical office will manually move the report to the Resolved state. 


C. CITIZEN UPDATES 
To strengthen trust between citizens and institutions, the citizen can receive updates regarding 
their own reports through various channels. First, at every state change, the citizen receives a 
notification on the platform with the corresponding update. Furthermore, municipal operators 
updating reports can send the reporting citizen a message through the platform, to which it can 
reply. The system must allow this functionality to be accessible by external chatbots as well. Each 
time the citizen receives a notification on the platform, they also get an email (this option can be 
disabled in the user settings panel, where they can also upload a personal photo). 
Moreover, after the approval phase, accepted reports immediately become visible on the 
Participium portal: they appear both on an interactive map of Turin, geolocated based on the 
citizen’s selected point, and in a summary table that allows filtering and sorting reports by 
category, status, or date. In both views, the reporter’s name (“anonymous” if that option was 
chosen) and the report title are displayed. Clicking on the title opens a page with the description.  
Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table. Once logged into 
Participium, citizens can follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications (following the 
same rules as for their own reports). 


D. STATISTICS 
The system allows viewing public and private statistics. Public statistics are visible in a dedicated 
section of the website and concern the number of reports per category, and trends over day, week, 
or month. They are also visible to non-registered users. In the private section, accessible only to 
administrators, it is possible to view, in addition to the public statistics, charts and tables.

highLevelGoals: Citizens should be able to submit detailed reports about urban problems, including location, description, category, and supporting photos, to the public administration.
Citizens should receive notifications and emails regarding status changes and messages related to their submitted reports, fostering trust and transparency.
Citizens should have the option to submit reports anonymously, protecting their privacy while still contributing to urban improvement.
Citizens should be able to track the progress and status of other citizens' public reports, promoting community awareness and engagement.
Organization Office Staff should be able to efficiently review, accept, or reject citizen reports to ensure their validity and appropriateness for further processing.
Organization Office Staff must provide mandatory written explanations for rejected reports to maintain transparency and citizen trust.
Technical Office Staff should be able to track and update the status of accepted reports through various stages, from 'In Progress' to 'Resolved', ensuring efficient issue resolution.
Technical Office Staff should be able to assign accepted reports to the appropriate internal technical offices or external maintenance companies based on the problem category.
Technical Office Staff should be able to exchange private comments and information with external maintenance personnel regarding specific reports.
External Maintenance Workers should be able to access reports assigned to them, update their status, and mark them as resolved upon completion of work.
External Maintenance Workers should be able to exchange private information and comments with the Technical Office Staff regarding the progress of assigned reports.
The Municipal Administrator should be able to configure the system to automatically assign reports of certain categories to external companies, streamlining the workflow.
The Municipal Administrator should be able to view detailed private statistics, including charts and tables, to monitor system performance and identify trends.
Public Viewers should be able to view accepted reports on an interactive map and in a summary table, promoting transparency and public awareness of urban problems.
Public Viewers should be able to access public statistics, such as the number of reports per category and trends over time, to understand the overall state of urban environment management.

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The provided high-level goals are comprehensive, accurate, and well-aligned with the software description. They correctly cover the functional requirements for all identified actors (Citizens, Organization Office, Technical Office, External Workers, Administrators, and Public Viewers). The goals appropriately abstract the 'why' and 'what' of the system (e.g., enabling reporting, managing lifecycle, ensuring transparency) without diving into low-level technical implementation details. There are no contradictions or significant omissions regarding the functional scope described in the text.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals:
[Citizen -> Enable citizens to report urban inconveniences] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a minor contradiction. 
1. **Contradiction**: The goal `UploadReportPhoto` states that the citizen must upload "up to three mandatory image files". The description explicitly states "It is also mandatory to attach one or more photos (up to 3 per report)". Therefore, the goal should reflect that at least one photo is mandatory, not that all three are mandatory.
2. **Omissions**: Several functional capabilities described in the software description are missing from the low-level goals:
   - **Viewing Public Reports**: The description states that "Even non-registered users can view both the maps and the summary table" and citizens can view the portal. There is no goal for viewing the public map or the public summary table of reports.
   - **Following Other Citizens' Reports**: The description mentions citizens can "follow other citizens’ open reports and receive notifications". There are no goals for following/unfollowing reports or receiving notifications for followed reports.
   - **User Settings**: The description mentions a "user settings panel" where users can disable email notifications and upload a personal photo. There are no goals for managing these settings.
   - **Viewing Statistics**: The description mentions public statistics are visible to non-registered users and citizens. There is no goal for viewing public statistics.

[Citizen -> Provide citizens with updates on their reports] Major omission and misalignment. The provided low-level goals only address the "Citizen Updates" aspect (notifications, viewing public reports, following reports). They completely fail to address the core functionality of the system: **Report Submission** (selecting map point, filling form, attaching photos, choosing anonymity) and **User Registration** (sign up, email confirmation). Furthermore, the high-level goal provided is too narrow ("Provide citizens with updates"), which causes the low-level goals to be incomplete relative to the full software description. The low-level goals should include actions like "Register new account", "Confirm registration via email link", "Submit new report with location and photos", and "View personal report details". Additionally, some low-level goals (like filtering/sorting public reports) are arguably better suited under a "View Public Reports" high-level goal rather than "Provide updates", though they are functionally correct. The primary issue is the missing submission and registration workflows.

[Citizen -> Allow citizens to control report anonymity] Major omission. The provided low-level goals only address the anonymity feature, completely ignoring the core functionalities of the system described in the software description, such as user registration, report submission (including map selection, form filling, and photo attachment), report lifecycle management, and receiving updates/notifications. Additionally, the actors list is incomplete, missing critical actors like the Municipality Administrator, Technical Office, and External Maintenance Personnel, which are necessary to fully represent the system. The high-level goals are also severely limited, focusing only on anonymity rather than the broader objective of enabling citizen participation in urban management.

[Citizen -> Enable citizens to follow public reports] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a significant omission. The high-level goal is "Enable citizens to follow public reports," and the description explicitly states that citizens can "follow other citizens’ open reports." However, the low-level goals only cover browsing, filtering, searching, and viewing details of public reports. They completely miss the core functionality of *following* (subscribing to) a specific report, which is the primary action implied by the high-level goal. While there is a goal to "Subscribe to status updates," it is framed generically and does not explicitly link to the act of following a specific public report as a distinct user action separate from just viewing it. More critically, the system description mentions that citizens can receive updates on *their own* reports and *followed* reports, but the low-level goals do not distinguish between the two or provide a clear mechanism for a citizen to initiate the "follow" action on a report they did not submit. The current set of goals describes a read-only browsing experience rather than an interactive following experience. Additionally, the goal "Send status update notification" is a system action, not a user action, and should be framed as the system's responsibility triggered by the user's follow action, but the user's action to *initiate* the follow is missing or poorly defined.

[Organization Office Staff -> Facilitate preliminary review of citizen reports] Input text must contain Feedback: ... and a final Score: line.

[Organization Office Staff -> Ensure clear communication for rejected reports] The provided low-level goals are severely incomplete and contain significant errors. 
1. **Major Omissions**: The goals completely ignore the core functionality for the primary actor, the Citizen. While there are a few goals for registration and submission, they miss critical features: viewing the public map/table (available to non-registered users), filtering/sorting reports, following other citizens' reports, receiving in-platform notifications, replying to messages from municipal operators, and managing user settings (disabling emails, uploading photos). 
2. **Actor Mismatch**: The input lists only "Organization Office Staff" as an actor, yet the low-level goals reference "Citizen", "Technical Office Staff", "External Maintenance Personnel", "System", and "Administrator". This inconsistency makes the model invalid.
3. **Incorrect Attribution**: Goals like `DisplayReportsOnMap` and `DisplayReportsInTable` are assigned to the "Administrator", but the description states these views are available to all users (including non-registered ones) for public reports. 
4. **Missing Functional Goals**: There are no goals for the Technical Office to assign reports to external companies (Case 1), nor for the system to handle the "Suspended" state logic correctly (the description says it's for organizational/technical reasons, not necessarily requiring a mandatory reason in the UI, though the goal adds a constraint not explicitly in the text, which is minor compared to the omissions).
5. **Contradiction**: The high-level goals provided in the prompt are extremely limited (only one goal for Organization Office Staff), yet the low-level goals reference many other high-level goals that were not provided in the input context. This suggests the assistant hallucinated the high-level goals or the input was truncated, but based on the provided text, the low-level goals do not align with the provided high-level goals.

[Technical Office Staff -> Manage the lifecycle of accepted reports] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical contradiction. 
1. **Contradiction**: The goal "Filter accepted reports by status" includes "Pending Approval" in its description. However, the high-level goal is to manage the lifecycle of *accepted* reports, and the system description states that "Pending Approval" reports are handled by the Organization Office, not the Technical Office. The Technical Office only sees reports after they are accepted (moved to "In Progress"). Including "Pending Approval" in the filter for the Technical Office is incorrect.
2. **Omissions**: The description explicitly states that "Staff from the technical office and external maintenance workers can exchange information and comments through the report". While there is a goal to "Add an internal comment", there is no goal for the Technical Office Staff to *view* or *read* the comments/updates provided by external maintenance workers. This is a critical part of the interaction and lifecycle management.
3. **Omissions**: The description mentions that the Technical Office assigns reports to the "technical office responsible, based on the problem category". While there is a goal to assign to an internal technician, the specific logic of assignment based on category is not explicitly captured as a distinct functional requirement or constraint in the low-level goals, though it might be implied. More importantly, the ability to *view* the external worker's updates is missing.

[Technical Office Staff -> Assign reports to responsible parties] The provided low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical contradiction regarding the report lifecycle. 
1. **Contradiction/Logic Error**: The high-level goal is to "Assign reports to responsible parties." According to the description, reports are assigned *after* approval, moving from "Pending Approval" to "In Progress". However, the low-level goal "Retrieve Unassigned In Progress Reports" implies that reports are already in the "In Progress" state *before* assignment. This contradicts the workflow where assignment happens *at* the transition to "In Progress" or immediately after. The system should retrieve reports in "Pending Approval" (if auto-assignment is configured) or newly approved reports to assign them.
2. **Major Omissions**: The high-level goal description explicitly states that Technical Office Staff are responsible for "updating their resolution status." The provided low-level goals only cover the assignment phase and moving to "Work in Progress." They completely omit the critical actions of:
   - Updating the status to "Suspended".
   - Updating the status to "Resolved" (closing the report).
   - Handling the specific case where external companies do *not* have access (manual update by staff).
   - Exchanging comments with external maintenance personnel (only adding comments is listed, not viewing/receiving them, though this might be part of the interaction).
3. **Scope**: The goals are too narrowly focused on the assignment mechanism and miss the broader lifecycle management responsibilities defined in the actor description and high-level goal.

[Technical Office Staff -> Facilitate internal communication on reports] The low-level goals are incomplete and contain a logical error in goal association. 
1. **Missing Goals**: The actor "Technical Office Staff" has significant responsibilities described in the system description (Section B) that are not covered by the provided low-level goals. Specifically, the staff must:
   - Assign reports to the responsible technical office based on category (currently, the goal "Assign a report..." exists but is incorrectly associated with the communication high-level goal, and the specific logic of assigning to the *responsible office* vs *external personnel* is conflated).
   - Manually move reports to "Resolved" for external companies without system access (Case 2). While "Manually close a resolved report" exists, it is also incorrectly associated with the communication goal.
   - The high-level goal provided is only "Facilitate internal communication". However, the actor's primary role is managing the report lifecycle (assignment, status updates, closing). There is a missing high-level goal for "Manage report lifecycle and assignment" or similar, which would properly house the goals for assigning, updating status, and closing reports.
2. **Incorrect Association**: The goals "Assign a report...", "Update the lifecycle status...", and "Manually close..." are functional actions related to workflow management, not just "internal communication". Associating them solely with "Facilitate internal communication" is semantically incorrect. They should be associated with a goal related to managing the report workflow/lifecycle.
3. **Scope**: The prompt asks to critique the work on defining low-level end-user goals. The provided set only covers a subset of the actor's actions (communication and some lifecycle steps) but fails to provide a coherent structure where lifecycle management is distinct from communication.

[External Maintenance Worker -> Enable external personnel to manage assigned reports] The low-level goals are well-structured and correctly identify the functional actions available to the External Maintenance Worker (authentication, viewing assigned reports, commenting, updating status to 'In Progress', and marking as 'Resolved'). However, there is a minor omission regarding the visibility of comments. The description explicitly states that comments exchanged between the technical office and external maintenance workers are "not visible to the reporting citizen (nor to other citizens)". While the current goal "View Report Comments/Information Exchange" implies viewing the relevant comments, it does not explicitly enforce the constraint that these comments are restricted from public/citizen view, which is a key functional requirement for this actor's interaction. Additionally, the goal "Add Completion Notes to Resolved Report" is slightly redundant or ambiguous; the description says the worker "can mark the report as resolved", and while adding notes is a reasonable inference for "exchange information", it is not explicitly mandated as a separate step distinct from the resolution action in the text (unlike the mandatory written explanation for rejections by the Organization Office). The main issue is the lack of explicit handling for the restricted visibility of the communication channel in the low-level goals, which is a critical functional aspect of the system design for this actor.

[External Maintenance Worker -> Facilitate communication with technical office staff] Major omission. The provided low-level goals only address the communication aspect (reading and writing comments) for the External Maintenance Worker. However, the software description explicitly states that external maintenance personnel can "move the report from Assigned to In Progress" and "mark the report as resolved." These are critical functional actions defined in the system's lifecycle (Section B, Case 1) and are completely missing from the low-level goals. Additionally, the high-level goals provided are extremely narrow, focusing solely on communication, which fails to represent the full scope of the actor's capabilities (status management) as described in the text. To improve, add low-level goals for updating the report status to "In Progress" and "Resolved," and ensure the high-level goals reflect the broader objective of managing assigned interventions.
